data.long_meaning: Amodh is derived from the Sanskrit word 'amodha' which means 'immeasurable', 'boundless', 'endless'. In Hindu mythology, Amodh is the name of a celestial elephant that supports the world on its back. The name Amodh carries the meaning “Immeasurable, Boundless” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amodh usually hope their child will grow to embody immeasurable, boundless and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amodh total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: Amodh was a famous Hindu prince and poet of the 11th century, who is believed to have lived in the kingdom of Kannauj in present-day Uttar Pradesh, India. He is best known for his contribution to the Sanskrit poetic tradition through his works in the Bhakti genre, which focused on devotion to the Hindu deity Krishna.

historical_references.reference: Amodh is also mentioned in the 13th-century Hindu epic, the Mahabharata, as a learned scholar and philosopher who was a disciple of the great sage Vyasa. He is credited with being one of the principal compilers of the Mahabharata, and his contributions to the epic include the Bhagavad Gita, which is considered one of the most influential Hindu texts.
